Reflexive verbs use sich: sich verstehen (to get on), sich streiten (to argue). Pronoun matches subject.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 1: People and Lifestyle (Identity and Relationships; Healthy Living and Lifestyle; Education and Work) — a core area of GCSE German.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 1: People and Lifestyle (Identity and Relationships; Healthy Living and Lifestyle; Education and Work) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 1: People and Lifestyle (Identity and Relationships; Healthy Living and Lifestyle; Education and Work).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I get on well with my mother'?
options: Ich verstehe mich gut mit meiner Mutter.
Ich verstehe mich gut mit meine Mutter.
Ich verstehe mir gut mit meiner Mutter.
Ich verstehen mich gut mit meine Mutter.

mcqs.q: Which form of 'you' do you use addressing a German teacher?
options: Sie
du
ihr
es

mcqs.q: When addressing a stranger or someone older formally, which 'you' do you use?
options: Sie (always capitalised, formal singular and plural).
Ihr.
Du - because it sounds friendly.
Ich will is future tense.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between 'ich will' and 'ich möchte'?
options: Ihr.
Ich will is future tense.
They mean the same thing.
Ich will = I want (strong, direct); ich möchte = I would like (polite).
Ihr.
To receive/get.
To begin.
To become.
